claims.text: About 250 million years ago, nearly all of Earth's land was joined in the supercontinent Pangaea.
Gondwana was the southern part of Pangaea and Laurasia the northern part, and Rodinia was a much older supercontinent that broke up hundreds of millions of years earlier.
The name Pangaea comes from Greek words meaning 'all the Earth'.
Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift in 1912.
Continental drift became widely accepted in the 1960s, with the development of plate tectonics.
